source.title: Uncovering ecological state dynamics with hidden Markov models

confidence_rationale: Comprehensive, authoritative review by leading movement-ecology statisticians of hidden Markov models (HMMs) as the field's standard rigorous tool for inferring latent behavioral states from tracking/movement data -- directly on-point for the source thought's informal state-transition language (refuge/explore/food-seeking states) and its request for 'validated measures of sequence structure.' Rated mixed rather than purely supports because the paper is equally explicit about documented failure modes in exactly this class of method, which speak directly to the anti-Goodharting risk GOV-BEHADJ-1 raises for hand-picked metrics -- the same risk recurs, in a different form, in model-based state discovery. High confidence given the source's authority and very close conceptual match to the claim's subject matter.
failure_signatures: 'The decision of the appropriate number of states can be challenging; there is again no foolproof or automatic way to determine this' -- state-count selection in HMM-based behavioral segmentation is a documented open problem, not a solved one, directly analogous to the metric-choice Goodharting risk the source thought raises.

When the transition matrix is fully free-parameterized, 'the characteristics of the model states as represented by the state-dependent distributions are fully data driven, and hence may not correspond exactly to biologically meaningful entities' -- i.e. an unsupervised or semi-supervised discovery pass can output statistically coherent 'states' that are model artifacts rather than real behavioral categories, a known failure mode in behavioural classification directly requested by the source thought's literature-mining instructions.

'Coarse-graining could result in masking or misclassification of meaningfully distinct states' when approximating a continuous behavioral space with too few discrete states -- and conditional-independence violations (observation at time t depending on the observation at t-1, not just the hidden state at t) can further confound behavioral inference if unaddressed.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Hidden Markov models provide the standard statistically rigorous framework in movement ecology for inferring discrete latent behavioral states (e.g. resting, foraging, transiting) from continuous tracking data, incorporating covariates and autocorrelation, but the review documents substantial open methodological challenges: state-number selection has no automatic solution, free-parameterized models can produce data-driven 'states' with no biological correspondence, and coarse-graining or conditional-independence violations can distort inference.
mapping.ree_translation: This paper is the single most direct match in the pull to the source thought's own informal proposal (refuge/explore/food-seeking/acquisition/return as discrete states with transitions between them, reversal frequency and excursion duration as pre-specified metrics). It confirms HMMs are the established, more rigorous formal machinery for exactly this kind of claim -- but its documented pitfalls should be read as a direct extension of GOV-BEHADJ-1's own anti-Goodharting checklist: if REE were to formalize its discovery-oriented channel using HMM-family models, the review's caution about data-driven states lacking real-world (for REE, functional) correspondence is precisely the same risk the source thought raises for hand-picked scalar metrics, now recurring at the level of MODEL SELECTION rather than metric selection. Any REE skill built from GOV-BEHADJ-1 should treat 'how many states did the model discover, and were they validated as functionally meaningful rather than merely statistically convenient' as its own checklist item.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The review's domain is animal movement ecology (GPS/accelerometer tracking of wild animals), which shares REE's interest in state-transition structure but not its computational substrate or its access to ground-truth internal state (REE, unlike a wild animal, could in principle inspect internal policy/value representations directly, which movement ecology cannot -- so some of the review's caution about state interpretability may be less severe for REE if internal-state cross-validation is available, and more severe if it is not used).
mapping.source_context: Methodological review synthesizing hidden Markov model applications across animal movement ecology, covering model specification, state-number selection, covariate inclusion, autocorrelation handling, and known limitations, aimed at practitioners applying HMMs to infer behavioral states from tracking data.

confidence_components.notes: Authoritative review by the field's leading methodologists in a top ecology journal, published 2020 and reflecting current best practice and known limitations. Mapping fidelity relatively high because the review's central subject -- inferring discrete behavioral states with transition structure from movement/tracking data -- is structurally close to what GOV-BEHADJ-1 itself proposes for REE trajectories.
